question.text: 'Vatsalya Charitable Society' runs a child-welfare centre with Rs 50 lakh annual budget, 12 trained teachers, a nutrition-kit supplier contract, and uses these to deliver daily meals, tuition classes and health check-ups to 500 children. In the logic-model taxonomy, money, teachers and supplier contracts represent which category?

answer.text: Inputs — the resources (human, financial, material) that go into the programme

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.5.1 (x), Inputs are the resources that go into the project/programme — human, financial and material (money, raw material, training material, technology). Rs 50 lakh, 12 teachers and supplier contracts are all inputs. The Trap: Option A (Outputs) would be the 500 children served, meals delivered. Option B (Outcomes) is the short-term learning/health improvement. Option D (Impact) is the long-term socio-emotional change. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to Ch 4 (Logic Model). The input-activity-output-outcome-impact chain is the backbone of SROI and all SAS standards. Assessor's Pro-Tip: In your SIR/AIR, present the logic chain as a table with each row tagged to a SAS indicator. Make input-side monetisation explicit (volunteer hours at shadow price) — auditors will ask for Input completeness when reviewing SROI denominators.
